findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer dispenser in the Winter utility closet was observed to be dispensing no measurable concentration of sanitizer. CORRECTED- maintenance was able to reconnect a hose that had come loose. Dispenser was observed to be releasing 400 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure frequent testing of chemical sanitizers to ensure the proper concentration as recommended by the manufacturer’s label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The test strips in the Reach kitchen were observed to have expired in 2021. CORRECTED- new sanitizer test strips were brought to each care center kitchen. Test kits must be available and functioning (periodically check expiration dates) to test the concentration of chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an accumulation of food and other debris in the following areas:
1) The corner cabinet in Summer.
2) Along the freezer gasket in Winter.
3) Along the freezer gasket in Spring.
4) In containers holding clean utensils in Spring.
5) In containers holding clean utensils in Reach.
6) The top of the Care Center dish machine.
Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed opened milk containers in both the Reach and Spring kitchen to be missing date marking. The person in charge (PIC) verified that they were opened within the past 1-2 days. CORRECTED- the date the items were opened was placed on the containers. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are date marked if held for over 24 hours. The date of opening/ preparation/ thawing counts as day one.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an unmarked bottle of clear liquid in the mop room of the Spring kitchen. The PIC was unable to verify the contents. CORRECTED- the bottle was emptied and brought to the main kitchen for ware washing. Ensure all clear liquids, chemicals, and cleaning products are labeled to prevent potential chemical contamination of foods or food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf[

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: The kitchen sanitizer bucket in the “Winter” wing was observed with no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- sanitizer bucket was remade and observed to be at a proper concentration of 400ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer buckets are changed at a frequency to hold proper concentration levels as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration of 200-400 ppm and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed food debris or dust in the following locations:
1) Food debris in the silverware divider in “Spring” kitchen
2) Food debris in the silverware divider in “Winter” kitchen
3) Dust and soil accumulation on top of the Care Center dish machine. 
Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of dust, soil, and food debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a leak on the front right edge of the Care Center’s dish machine during the rinse cycle. The person in charge (PIC) was notified and will be making a call to EcoLab to have the machine serviced. Ensure plumbing systems are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector and PIC observed holes in the walls (appeared as through shelving units had been relocated) of the mop sink rooms in each branch of the Care Center. The PIC noted the repairs to be made by maintenance. Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Slight soil accumulation was observed in the Memory Care and Spring ice machines. Ensure the interiors of ice machines are cleaned regularly to prevent soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: MEMORY CARE: The kitchen sanitizer bucket was observed with no measurable sanitizer concentration. The concentrated sanitizer jug on the dispenser was observed to be low and incapable of dispensing proeprly. CORRECTED- PIC replaced the concentrated jug with a new one. Sanitizer was then dispensed at 400ppm quat.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration of 200-400 ppm and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Dishwasher temperature logs in the SPRING Care Center were not available. Inspector will follow up to see that staff have been trained on how to properly complete the logs, and that the logs are being regularly and accurately completed.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Probe thermometers in the SUMMER kitchen were not accurate. One thermometer read 0F at room temperature. Another thermometer ready 35F when in ice water. CORRECTED- Thermometers were calibrated using ice water. Check thermometer calibration on a regular basis to ensure they are accurate to +/-2F.
4-203.11: (A) FOOD TEMP. MEASURING DEVICE shall be accurate to  +/- 1 Celsius (B) accurate to +/- 2 Fahrenheit.  [Pf]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Dishwasher temperature logs in the Memory Care Center were not available. Inspector will follow up to see that staff have been trained on how to properly complete the logs, and that the logs are being regularly and accurately completed.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16. [Pf]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Dishwasher temperature logs in the Memory Care Center were found to be falsified. Logs for most of the month of August were already completed during this inspection (on August 1st). Inspector will follow up to see that staff have been trained on how to properly complete the logs, and again in several months to see that the logs are being regularly and accurately completed.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16. [Pf]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Forks and spoons observed at the Summer Care Center with food contact ends out. CORRECTED- Utensils were removed from the service counter. Discussed proper utensil storage (eating ends down). 
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.11 Food service staff working in Memory Care wing were unable to properly wash hands at the designated handwashing sink in the kitchen based on conditions observed. Pump bottle of hand sanitizer was present at the handwashing sink, and the automatic soap dispenser was not working properly (see #10 for details). Servers were noted to have washed their hands in the restroom prior to serving residents, which would require touching general surfaces not considered to be clean prior to service. Proper handwashing at the designated handwashing sink in the kitchen prior to service and between tasks was discussed. 
Food employees shall keep their hands and exposed portions of their arms clean.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 1. Automatic soap dispenser at handwashing sink in Memory Care kitchen was not functioning properly. A part was broken inside the dispenser that allows soap to dispense when activated. Maintenance changed the soap dispenser during inspection, and new dispenser functioned properly.
2. Soap would not dispense from automatic soap dispenser in the dish room. Batteries were changed to allow for proper function of the soap dispenser.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-302.12 Food thermometer was not present at Memory Care kitchen. PIC provided new thermometer during inspection.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee working in Spring Hill kitchen did not wash hands between taking a drink from a personal beverage and putting on gloves to continue with next task. Handwashing between tasks and prior to putting on gloves were discussed. Employee was observed washing hands properly between tasks for remainder of inspection.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, after handling soiled equipment and utensils, before putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold was observed in the Summer Breeze, Spring Hill, and Reach kitchen ice machines on front surfaces around the ice maker covers. Mold was also observed on the sides of the water trough in back of the Summer Breeze ice machine. Ensure ice machines are cleaned and sanitized as needed to prevent mold growth.
Equipment such as ice bins and enclosed components, such as ice makers, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle in the Memory Care kitchen was observed with a label indicting it was QT 3 hard surface disinfectant. Employee working in Memory Care stated the bottle contained Re-Juv-Nal quat sanitizer that is used in the kitchens. Proper labeling was discussed, and employee stated they would relabel the bottle. Although QT 3 and Re-Juv-Nal are both quat products they have different intended uses. QT 3 is a hard surface disinfectant and Re-Juv-Nal is sanitizer intended for use in kitchens. Make sure chemicals are in properly labeled spray bottles and used appropriately based on the intended use of chemicals.
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Evidence was observed to indicate a handwashing sink was used as a dump sink. Ice cubes were observed in the basin of the Memory Care kitchen handwashing sink. Manager was advised to speak with all staff about proper use of handwashing sinks. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using handwashing sinks as dump sinks.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Ice machines in all four kitchens had varying amounts of mold growth on inner surfaces. The ice machines in Memory Care, Spring Hill, and Reach had the most buildup. Ensure ice machines are cleaned and sanitized as needed to prevent mold growth.
Equipment such as ice bins and enclosed components, such as ice makers, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.112 Main dish machine rinse gauge was observed at ~198F (almost 200F) during the final rinse cycle. Manager called for service to get the dish machine serviced. 
In a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 194F.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Probes of food thermometers were soiled with stuck on food debris in the REACH kitchen. Food thermometers were cleaned during inspection. Cleaning frequency was discussed. Ensure properly cleaning and sanitizing of food thermometer probes between uses.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes are used to wipe food thermometers, then make sure probes are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottles in the Memory Care kitchen were incorrectly labeled as to the contents. Labels were for peroxide disinfectant cleaner and a QT3 product, and both bottles container Re-Juv-Nal quat sanitizer. Contents were emptied from the bottles. Ensure proper labeling of all chemical spray bottles. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was not available for checking sanitizer solutions in Memory Care kitchen. Test strips were provided. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following general surfaces were soiled in the Memory Care kitchen:
1. Bottom inside right freezer (food splash); and 
2. Inside cabinet used for storage of cooking spray (general buildup).
Clean inside all fridges, freezers, and cabinets daily/as needed throughout the facility.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Freshly dispensed sanitizer solution in a sani-bucket was observed at 0ppm quat in the AL memory care kitchen. The chemical jug hooked up at the dispenser was empty. PIC had cook obtain solution from the Summer kitchen until product could be replaced. PIC spoke with a member of housekeeping staff about replacing the product. Housekeeping will educate kitchen staff on where to find replacement product and how to change at the dispenser.  
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Ice machines in AL memory care, Summer, and Reach kitchens were all observed with mold growth on inner surfaces. Ensure ice machines are cleaned and sanitized as needed to prevent mold growth.
Equipment such as ice bins and enclosed components, such as ice makers, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-502.11 DISH ROOM - Wash gauge on the dish machine was not working. The gauge did not move at all after a half dozens cycles. Call for service was made during the inspection. 
Water temperature measuring devices shall be maintained in good repair and be accurate within the intended range of use.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sani-buckets were not setup and available for use in the AL memory care and Reach kitchens. Staff were advised on setup and use of sanitizer solution during hours of operation. 
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the handsink in the Summer kitchen. Handwashing poster was located and placed at the handsink.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Fruit salad containing sliced melons was observed with surface and internal temperatures of 54F-59F. Fruit salad was prepared earlier in the morning, brought over from the main kitchen and left our during part of breakfast service. Remaining portion of fruit salad was discarded.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was not available for checking sanitizer solutions in Summer kitchen. A new set of test strips was provided during inspection. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Bottom inside drawers and cabinets in Summer and REACH kitchens were observed with varying amounts of splash and general buildup. Ensure the surfaces inside cabinets and drawers are getting cleaned as needed to eliminate buildup.
Also, along the bottom of the ice machine doors had some buildup of splash and dust. Clean the lower surfaces of the ice machine/bottom of the doors inside and out as needed to minimize buildup of splash and dust.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Stems of food thermometers were soiled with old food debris buildup at the winter kitchen. Use and general maintenance of thermometers were discussed. Thermometers in question were set aside for cleaning. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes or sanitizer solution are used to wipe the thermometer probe during temperature checks, make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Scoop was observed inside the ice machine with the handle down inside touching ice at the winter kitchen. The scoop was moved and placed in the proper holding compartment inside the machine. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, such as ice scoops, shall be stored in a clean, protected location.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Quat solution in Summer kitchen sani-bucket was at 0ppm. The chemical bottle at the dispenser was found to be empty and little to no product in the bottom. A new bottle of chemical was connected at the dispenser, and freshly dispensed quat solution was observed at 200-400ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.
Make sure chemical bottles are changed as product gets low and is no longer dispensing at proper concentration. Maintain quat solutions at 200-400ppm as directed by the label instructions.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.12 Microwave in Spring kitchen had dried food splash inside. Clean inside microwaves as needed/at minimum up to every 24hrs.
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14  Employee in Winter kitchen was observed wiping crumbs out of the hot holding drawer with a dry wiping cloth and then placing said wiping cloth in the back pocket of her pants. Also, a spray bottle of sanitizer was available for use. Proper use and storage of wiping cloths were discussed. Soiled cloths were placed in the laundry bag for washing. 

Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at the required concentration of product used for sanitizing. Dry wiping cloths shall be free of food debris and visible soil.
Use disposable paper towels with spray bottles of sanitizer and discard paper towels after use. If wiping cloths are used, then they need to be stored in a sanitizer solution between uses. Used wiping cloths should not be hanging from belt loops and/or pockets due to the potential to re-use and the potential to create a source of cross contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Cabinets used for storage of garbage cans had varying amounts of buildup of food debris/splash inside. Clean the garbage can cabinets daily/as needed.

Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13 Mop bucket containing waste water from cleaning the previous evening was observed  the Winter kitchen mop closet. Proper disposal of waste water after use was discussed. Soiled mop water was discarded during the inspection.
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. Properly dispose of mop water after use and do not leave it sitting in the facility overnight.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-305.11 An employee's coat and purse were observed on the chemical shelving in the Spring kitchen mop closet. Employee working in that kitchen was not present; proper storage of personal items was discussed with manager. 
Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Sliced cantaloupe in one of the REACH kitchen fridges had a date mark of 11/11. Bags of deli turkey and ham in one of the Summer kitchen fridges were without date marks. All items were discarded. Make sure products are clearly labeled and not held longer than 7 days under refrigeration once opened/prepared. 

Refrigerated, ready to eat foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) and held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Solution in a spray bottle labeled as sanitizer in the REACH mop closet was at 0ppm quat. Another spray bottle also labeled sanitizer in the same mop closet that was almost empty was observed at 200ppm quat. The bottle containing diluted solution was emptied during the inspection. 

Maintain quat solutions at proper concentration per the label instructions. Use test strips to verify proper concentration, as solution concentration will weaken over time even when stored in a sealed spray bottle. Change solutions in spray bottles as needed based on use and the concentration observed when checked with test strips.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Sliced deli turkey had a date of 7/24 in the Spring kitchen, and open cottage cheese in the Summer kitchen had a date mark of 7/23. Both products were discarded during the inspection. 
Make sure products are clearly labeled (received date versus open date) and not held longer than 7 days under refrigeration once opened/prepared. 

Refrigerated, ready to eat foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) and held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - A spray bottle labeled Multi-Quat sanitizer in the Summer mop closet was at 0ppm. The main chemical bottle connected to the dispenser was empty. A new bottle was connected, and the solution was observed at 200ppm when the bottle was refilled. Also, what appeared to be a used wiping cloth was observed hanging on another spray bottle in the same mop closet. The spray bottle in question was not labeled but confirmed to be sanitizer with the use of a test strip. Wiping cloth was placed in the soiled linen laundry bag.
Maintain quat solutions at proper concentration per the label instructions and do not use wiping cloths with spray bottles. Use disposable paper towels and discard after use when spray bottles of sanitizer are in use. 

The wiping cloth in the Spring kitchen sani-bucket was not submerged in solution. The amount of solution was not adequate to allow for proper storage of the wiping cloth between uses. Make sure the sani-buckets have enough sanitizer to allow for submersion of wiping cloths in solution for proper storage between uses.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1280 - A pair of jeans was observed to be stored on top of clean wiping cloths in the REACH mop closet. Jeans were moved to the lower shelf of the storage cart away from clean linens.

An adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
(R) 750.1300 - Spray bottles in Spring and Summer mop closets were without proper labels. Both were verified to be sanitizer with the use of test strips. Spring bottle just had SPRING written on it twice and was labeled with the word sanitizer also. Manager emptied the chemical from the Summer wing bottle and discarded the bottle in the trash.

Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750.120 & 250 - Hashbrowns on the counter by the stove in the Winter kitchen had an internal temperature of 68°F. Employee stated hashbrowns are normally held in the cooler and just pulled out when needed, but he had not yet placed the product back in the fridge. Hashbrowns were discarded.
Liquid egg in the fridge was observed at 52°F in the Winter kitchen. Employee stated the product was out for use earlier that morning. Remainder of product was to be used through breakfast and any leftover portion would be discarded. 
Cold foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at 41°F/below at all times during storage. Discussed leaving larger container of hashbrowns, liquid egg, etc. in the fridge and maintaining a small working supply that will be used or discarded at breakfast time.
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Deli turkey in the Summer kitchen fridge had a date mark of 3/16. Turkey was discarded.
Refrigerated, ready to eat TCS foods held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded within 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
NOTE: Make sure all staff are dating in the same manner. For example, if the practice is to date mark the label with the date a food was prepared, then make sure all staff are maintaining the original date mark when foods are moved from the main kitchen to the satellite kitchens at the Care Center.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) inside microwaves in all kitchens (varying degree of food splash inside);   and
B) ice machine (REACH kitchen) - inner surfaces of right wall, front ledge, and door (coffee splash).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces at a frequency for the equipment in question to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1300 - Spray bottle in the Spring kitchen was labeled Orange Force but had sanitizer in it. Proper labeling of chemicals was discussed. Sanitizer was written on the label.

Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
(R) 750.510 - Employee in Winter Haven washed hands with proper technique but then proceeded to wipe hands with the paper towel after it was used to shut off the manual faucet. Proper technique was discussed with the employee, reiterating the importance of avoiding re-contamination of hands. If hands need to be dried further after the paper towel is used to shut off the manual faucet, then retrieve a new paper towel to finish drying hands.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket in the Winter Haven mop closet had a concentration of less than 100ppm quat. Employee stated the solution was just prepared recently, and the chemical bottle was changed prior to running the solution. Chemical was allowed to run through the line prior to refilling the bucket. The solution was then observed at 200ppm.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.
**When chemical bottles are switched out at the dispenser, run the solution for several seconds from the dispenser prior to filling sani-buckets and spray bottles. Also, when checking the concentration of the solution make sure the foam is settled out and the liquid is getting checked. Placing a test strip in the foam can result in a false read that may indicate the solution is at proper concentration when really it is not.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly

Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Maintain proper labels on chemical spray bottles.

Non-kitchen staff personnel entered the Reach kitchen and did not wash hands prior to retrieving juice and glasses to pour beverages for residents. Manager stated handwashing would be discussed with all staff. It is company policy that persons entering the kitchen must wash hands. Hands must definitely be washed prior to handling food/beverage containers, clean dishes, and unwrapped single service articles used of residents.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1280 - Employee purse was observed on the counter beneath the microwave in Spring Hill. Purse was moved to the mop closet and placed on the shelving with garbage bags and chemical bottles. 

Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage areas to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store personal items away from food prep/storage areas in the kitchens.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.citation_text:
750.1390 - Damp mop was observed in the basin of the Reach mopsink. Store mops hanging or inverted between uses to allow for proper drying of wet mop heads.

Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored properly.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750.120 & 250 - Temperature abuse of shell eggs and egg wash was observed in two out of the four kitchens.
1. Shell eggs in Winter Haven kitchen were observed in the fridge with surface temperatures of 48F-52F. Cook stated the flat of eggs was out while preparing food for some of the residents. An egg was cracked to obtain an internal temperature and observed to be at 55F. Breakfast was coming to an end, and the eggs would be discarded by 10a.
2. Egg was in the Reach kitchen had surface and internal temperatures of 52F and 57F respectively. Cook stated the product was out for a period of time while preparing food for residents. All remaining egg wash was to be discarded at the end of breakfast.

Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage, display and service. If it is easier to use time control, then establish and adhere to a time control policy for working supplies of eggs and egg wash (Time Control policy sheet provided).
findings.citation_text:
750.151(a) - 2. Gallon jugs of open milk in all four kitchens were observed with date marks of 2/20 and/or 2/19. Staff noted those were the dates the products were received, and all jugs of milk were opened either today or within the last two to three days based on information provided. The benefit of the doubt was given; all milks were re-dated and kept for use.
1. Potato salad in the Winter Haven fridge had a date mark of 2/19. Product was past the 7 day time frame for use. Container was placed on the cart to be taken to the main kitchen for product to be disposed of and container placed through ware washing.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded within 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Sausage links in the Winter Haven hot holding drawer were observed with a surface temperature of 112F. The hot holding drawer did not appear to be functioning properly. Manager advised the cook to use the oven for hot holding during other meals until the drawer could be serviced and repaired. Sausages were to be discarded at the end of breakfast.

Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135F/above at all times during storage, display and service.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Kitchen staff were observed going between tasks and changing gloves without washing hands. Several employees were also observed washing hands without proper technique. Employees were observed shutting off the manual faucets without a barrier and/or using the paper towel to shut off the faucet and then continued to dry hands with the same paper towels. Proper handwashing technique and when to wash hands were discussed with staff.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have become contaminated, prior to putting on gloves, between glove changes, and prior to handling food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. Educational handouts on proper handwashing and when to wash hands were provided.

750.160b - Cook put on a pair of gloves to handle food and did not change gloves after touching the fridge door handle. The handle had visible buildup on the front, and soil accumulation could be felt on the back side of the handle as well. Proper use of gloves and changing gloves between tasks were discussed.
  
Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations. Educational handout on proper glove use was provided.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - 1. In-use damp and/or dry wiping cloths were observed lying on counters in three out of the four kitchens. One Cook had a wiping cloth hanging from his belt loop and stated the cloth was used to wipe crumbs off the counter. Proper use and storage of wiping cloths were discussed with manager and staff at all four kitchens. 

2. Green bucket in the Summer Breeze kitchen was observed at 0ppm quat. Employee noted it was sanitizer solution obtained from the dispenser in the mop closet. The dispenser was set to all purpose cleaner. Employee was advised on proper use of the chemical dispenser (use quat solution to fill sani-bucket) and also advised to utilize red sanitation buckets for sanitizer solutions. Solution in question was discarded.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.
NOTE: If spray bottles of sanitizer are used, then paper towels must be utilized when wiping down surfaces. Paper towels must be discarded after each use. If wiping cloths are to be used, then a sanitizer solution must be maintained for storage of the wiping cloths in the solution between uses.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-151(a) Observed cheese slices and shreds in Winter Haven and Summer to not have date marking. Most other items within the coolers are observed with proper date marking. Discussed the date marking of milks. Most kitchens are going through gallons of milk within a day or two. findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-140b Observed a bag of corned beef with the date 2/26. Corned beef was from the Monday of this week. Bag was improperly labeled (or reused - cease this practiced). Also, observed an opened brick of brie cheese from sandwiches made earlier in the week. Discarded during the inspection. Discussed date marking with staff. Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a Observed opened bottled beverages being stored on the top shelf of cooler #1 in Spring. Moved to the lower shelf during the inspection. Cease storing opened beverages over ready-to-eat foods going to be served to residents. Store opened personal items so that if they spill they will not contaminate foods.  Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b One kitchen had a wet sani-cloth on the counter. Most of the kitchens use the spray bottles with paper towels. Discussed using a sani-bucket with staff. We have no preference for what you choose to use.  Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: 750-1060 The mop sink in Summer has a leak. Repair the leak. All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1200 The coving beneath the sinks in Winter has been pulled off. Replace the coving or eliminate the gap between kickplate pieces. Floor and surrounding surfaces should be maintained smooth and easily cleanable. The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-650a A turkey roasting pan was observed rusty and with flaking coating (Summer). The pan had not been used since Thanksgiving. Pan was pulled from service during the inspection. Make sure pans that have a peeling or flaking coating are removed from service.  Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
750-810b Spring Hill quat spray bottles were observed at 0ppm Quat. During the inspection, it was noted that a new bag of chemical had recently been changed in the wall-mounted unit. The system was not properly dispensing the right amount of chemical. The system had to be run for  some time before 200ppm Quat came through. Make sure that staff knows to 'prime' or run the chemical for several minutes after a bag is changed. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

ALSO: make sure that staff is storing wet wiping cloths within a sani-bucket of solution between uses. Observed a wet sani-cloth stored on a spray bottle. Spray bottles should be used with paper towels OR use the cloth for the cleaning of one service and then place in soiled linens. Grab a new towel for each clean-up. A wet wiping cloth should be stored in a bucket of solution between uses.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: 750-290 Observed the ice scoop handle to be stored in the ice (Spring Hill kitchen). During the inspection, the scoop was stored with handle extending out of the ice. Cease storing scoop so handle touches ice. Eliminate hand to food contact. Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a Observed an employee chewing gum while preparing food. Chewing gum increases the production of saliva. Cease chewing gum while preparing foods and working with equipment. Employee discarded gum during the inspection. Employees shall consume food, gum, and beverages only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Observed the shelf surrounding the floor drain from the dish machine in Spring Hill to be damaged and have peeling laminate. Discussed sanding and painting with Household Coordinator. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Sanitizing spray bottle tested at 0 ppm Quat in Spring Hill. The bottle was refilled and still found to be 0ppm Quat. Ecolab will be contacted to deal with the wall mounted dispensing problem. Sanitizing solution will be taken from an adjacent kitchen in the interim. Discussed the color of solution and the daily testing of sanitizing spray bottles. This particular bottle had a clear liquid content while every other quat bottle is tinted pink. Showed test kit to employees and discussed a proper solution of 200 ppm Quat. The sanitizing of surfaces is incredibly important in your sensitive population facility. Test solutions daily and educate staff. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Cabinet to the left of the dish machine in Summer is observed soiled with accumulation food debris. Throughout all four kitchens, the cabinet beneath the 2-part sinks are observed soiled and stained. Clean cabinets. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-140b Observed cheese slices without a proper date marking in Summer. Items were properly labeled during the inspection. Discussed the seven day rule. Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-130(d)  Observed eggs stored over juice in the refrigerators of Reach and Spring. Eggs were stored on the bottom shelf during the inspection. All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1200 The baseboard in Summer is observed damaged and incomplete. There are some areas where a quarter inch gap is visible between the baseboard and the flooring. Eliminate the gap between the floor and the baseboard. You may use painted or seal quarter-round, coving, baseboard, or caulking to eliminate this gap. The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.
